text_blocks.snippet: Polyuria, or excessive urination, is a common symptom of diabetes due to the body's attempt to rid itself of excess glucose and water. In diabetes, high blood sugar levels lead to glucose in the urine, which then draws water with it, resulting in increased urine production. This can lead to dehydration and increased thirst (polydipsia) as the body tries to compensate for the fluid loss.
snippet_highlighted_words: a common symptom of diabetes due to the body's attempt to rid itself of excess glucose and water

list.title: Diabetes and Glucose:
list.snippet: In both type 1 and type 2 diabetes, the body either doesn't produce enough insulin or can't properly use the insulin it produces, leading to high blood glucose (sugar) levels.

list.title: Kidneys and Glucose:
list.snippet: When blood glucose levels are high, the kidneys, which normally filter and reabsorb glucose, become overwhelmed.

list.title: Glucose in Urine:
list.snippet: If the glucose in the blood exceeds the kidneys' reabsorption capacity, excess glucose spills into the urine.
